Maya (Marketing): Hey runtime team — quick, concrete ask for the webinar next week. We need a small rerun focused on stability of latency percentiles and warmup behavior so we can confidently show p50/p95/p99 numbers in the deck. Deadline: EOD tomorrow if possible.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): OK — can you list the exact metrics + variants you want? Also do you need raw logs or just aggregated CSV?

Maya (Marketing): Aggregated CSV + a short raw-sample log (one file) is ideal. Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99, mean, stdev, plus cold-start vs warm (first 10 requests vs after warmup), token throughput (tokens/sec), GPU util, and request-level error counts.

Tina (Product Ops): Also call out model variants we plan to publish: baseline FP16, int8/quantized, and a small-fp16 variant used for canary. We want side-by-side numbers.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Got it. Propose the run matrix:
- Models: model-v1-fp16, model-v1-int8, model-v1-canary-fp16
- Payload cohorts: 60% short (<=32 tokens), 30% medium (~128 tokens), 10% long (~512 tokens)
- Warmup: 50 requests per worker OR 60s warmup, whichever hits first
- Batch sizes: config to reflect production routing (single-request + up to batch=8)

Sahil (Eng Runtime): For percentile stability we should capture at least 10k requests per variant (=> gives decent p99 signal). Can we do 10k across the cohorts? That means ~6k short, 3k medium, 1k long.

Maya (Marketing): 10k per variant is fine. We only plan to show p95 and p99 in the slides but want p50/p90 too for internal.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Cool. Deliverables I'll produce: aggregated CSV (one row per request with columns: variant, cohort, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, gpu_util, worker_id, warmed_flag), a summary table with p50/p90/p95/p99 and mean/stdev, and a short notes.txt describing methodology + any anomalies.

Maya (Marketing): Perfect. Can you also do a tiny sanity check comparing "cold-first-req" vs "steady-state" tail behavior for the canary? We want to call out any >20% delta at p99.

Sahil (Eng Runtime): Will do. Note: quantized runs may have higher variance on long sequences — we'll surface that.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): One more ask from runtime: please provide the exact sample generation command used by marketing to create the payload set (so we can reproduce). If you don't have it, we can generate a deterministic seed-based sample.

Maya (Marketing): Sample gen snippet (seeded):
```
python tools/sample_payloads.py --seed 42 --n 10000 \
  --distribution "short:0.6,mid:0.3,long:0.1" \
  --lengths "short:8,mid:128,long:512" --output payloads.jsonl
```
Use that.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Great — thanks. We'll run on dedicated ci-runtime pool to avoid noisy neighbors. Expected ETA: start tonight, finish tomorrow morning. If anything looks weird we'll ping here.

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1718884050 started on pool ci-runtime (owner: Lucas). Estimated runtime: ~2.5h per variant.

Tina (Product Ops): Please include a single-slide-friendly table and a one-sentence explanation of methodology for the comms review.

Sahil (Eng Runtime): Noted. Deliverables: payloads.jsonl (used), raw-sample.log (first 1k lines), aggregated.csv, summary_table.csv, methodology.txt, anomalies.md.

Maya (Marketing): Amazing — thanks team. If the quantized p99 is worse than FP16 by >20% we may drop the quantized claim from the launch notes, so call it out explicitly. :pray:

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Will highlight. We'll post results as a zip artifact in this thread when done.

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1718884050 completed. artifact: s3://redwood-bench/1718884050/results.zip

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Results uploaded. Quick summary: model-v1-int8 p99 delta vs fp16 = +12% (within threshold), canary-fp16 p99 = +4%. Long-cohort shows higher variance — see anomalies.md. Uploads: aggregated.csv, summary_table.csv, methodology.txt, anomalies.md, raw-sample.log.

Maya (Marketing): Received — reviewing now. Will take summary_table.csv and craft one slide. If anything else is needed we'll follow up. Thanks! :rocket:
